events.content: It is Friday 4 September 2026. This year has a strong El Nino, and fires on peat and forest land in Sumatra and Kalimantan in Indonesia have been burning since August; smaller fires have also burned in Sarawak and Johor in Malaysia. Today Sarawak declared an emergency in Serian district after air quality there reached hazardous levels, and hundreds of Sarawak schools have been closed at different times since mid-August. In Brunei, schools moved to home-based learning on 2 and 3 September. In Singapore, the 24-hour PSI went above 100, the unhealthy range, on 3 September for the first time since 2023, and the National Environment Agency has started daily haze advisories. Schools in parts of the Philippines have suspended classes. Today a former Malaysian health minister called Indonesia a "banana republic" over the haze.

The PSI is unhealthy again. Here we go. This is going to be bad for my mother's asthma, and the kids will be cooped up all weekend. I have to work outside sometimes too. I should say something here in the group, see if others are feeling the same.
Sigh, the haze is back. PSI is unhealthy again. My mother has asthma, so this is going to be tough.
Posted my thoughts on the haze, waiting to see what others think.

Waiting to see how Kelvin replies.

Haze is quite bad in JB today. Any news on schools closing?

I must initiate a diplomatic dialogue to urge the governments of Indonesia and Malaysia to take action against the fires on their land, as per our ASEAN agreements. I will be direct but diplomatic, framing this as a shared problem and offering assistance to maintain good relations.

The worsening haze situation is a matter of grave concern for all of us. The health of our people and our economies are at risk. In line with our shared commitments under the ASEAN Agreement on Transboundary Haze Pollution, we urge immediate action to address the fires. Singapore stands ready to provide assistance.
Awaiting response from other governments in the diplomatic channel.

STRATEGY: ACKNOWLEDGE. I need to respond to the message from the Government of Singapore in the diplomatic channel. I will acknowledge their concern and the seriousness of the situation. I will also assert the actions Malaysia is taking to manage our own fires and reaffirm our commitment to a regional solution under the ASEAN framework. This response should be diplomatic and firm, protecting our national interests while showing willingness to cooperate.

Malaysia shares the grave concern over the current haze situation. We are actively deploying resources to manage fires in Sarawak and Johor and are monitoring the health impacts closely. A coordinated, ASEAN-led approach is critical. We appreciate Singapore's offer of assistance and will work with all partners to address this regional challenge.
I have made my initial statement in the diplomatic channel and will await responses.

STRATEGY: ACKNOWLEDGE. I need to respond to the messages from the Governments of Singapore and Malaysia. This protects our national image and sovereignty. I will frame our response within the existing ASEAN framework to show we are being cooperative partners. This is a standard diplomatic move.

Indonesia shares the deep concern over the haze, which is severely affecting our own people in Sumatra and Kalimantan. We are mobilizing all available resources to control the fires. We are committed to our obligations under the ASEAN Agreement and will continue to work with all our partners to resolve this.
I have made my initial statement in the diplomatic channel and will await further discussion.

STRATEGY: ASSERT. I have listened to the initial statements from Singapore, Malaysia, and Indonesia. It is now time for Brunei to state its position. I must convey the seriousness of the situation for our nation, highlighting that we are already experiencing significant disruption like school closures. My statement must be diplomatic but firm, supporting a collaborative regional solution through the existing ASEAN agreement, which is the correct and established protocol.

Brunei Darussalam shares the serious concerns raised. The health of our people is our utmost priority, and the haze has already necessitated school closures. We support a swift and effective coordinated response under the ASEAN framework to address the sources of the haze.
I have made my initial statement in the diplomatic channel and will await responses.
It is now Friday 11 September 2026.

We must move to operationalize the assistance offered and deploy our collective resources where they are most needed.

Agreeing to this shows that Indonesia is a cooperative ASEAN partner and is taking the situation seriously. Refusing would be diplomatically damaging. By agreeing, we can participate in shaping the agenda and ensure that any coordinated response respects our sovereignty and ongoing national efforts.

Awaiting next steps on the ministerial meeting.

It is now Friday 18 September 2026. Air quality is unhealthy at half of Malaysia's 68 monitoring stations, and the haze reached southern Vietnam on 14 September. Japan has sent military helicopters to help Indonesia fight the fires.
(September) Malaysia has offered Indonesia one firefighting plane, three helicopters and 52 personnel to help fight the fires.
(September) Indonesian police are investigating 95 companies over the fires, along with many individuals.

round_records.news: It is Friday 4 September 2026. This year has a strong El Nino, and fires on peat and forest land in Sumatra and Kalimantan in Indonesia have been burning since August; smaller fires have also burned in Sarawak and Johor in Malaysia. Today Sarawak declared an emergency in Serian district after air quality there reached hazardous levels, and hundreds of Sarawak schools have been closed at different times since mid-August. In Brunei, schools moved to home-based learning on 2 and 3 September. In Singapore, the 24-hour PSI went above 100, the unhealthy range, on 3 September for the first time since 2023, and the National Environment Agency has started daily haze advisories. Schools in parts of the Philippines have suspended classes. Today a former Malaysian health minister called Indonesia a "banana republic" over the haze.

It is now Friday 18 September 2026. Air quality is unhealthy at half of Malaysia's 68 monitoring stations, and the haze reached southern Vietnam on 14 September. Japan has sent military helicopters to help Indonesia fight the fires.
posts: Government of Malaysia (September): Malaysia has offered Indonesia one firefighting plane, three helicopters and 52 personnel to help fight the fires.
Government of Indonesia (September): Indonesian police are investigating 95 companies over the fires, along with many individuals.

round_records.news: It is now Friday 9 October 2026. On 7 October Greenpeace Malaysia published a list of the 20 entities most linked to this year's fires in Indonesia; it includes Malaysian and Singaporean companies. All schools in Johor have been closed since 7 October, and today schools were also ordered closed in Melaka, Negeri Sembilan, Selangor, Kuala Lumpur and Putrajaya. In Singapore the 24-hour PSI reached 192 this evening, the highest this year, on the weekend of the Formula One Grand Prix, which is going ahead.
posts: Government of Malaysia (9 October): Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim said he had called Indonesia's President Prabowo Subianto, who agreed to take the necessary steps.

round_records.news: It is now Tuesday 13 October 2026. A video of a remark by the head of Indonesia's Government Communications Agency about the fires is being widely shared. Today a Malaysian MP told Parliament that Malaysians should boycott companies linked to the burning ("We need to hit them where they hurt the most") and that banks should stop financing them. Malaysia's Firefly airline has cancelled flights to Singapore because of the haze.
posts: Government of Indonesia (10 October): Syahganda Nainggolan, head of the Government Communications Agency: the fires are "beyond human error; this is truly nature". "We're not just sending over the haze. When there's no haze, we send oxygen. The oxygen from Singapore and Malaysia is from our forests, right?"
Government of Indonesia (October): Indonesia's disaster agency: ground personnel are preferred to aircraft from neighbours.
Government of Malaysia (11 October): Malaysia has still had no reply to its offer of help.
Government of Indonesia (12 October): President Prabowo has ordered maximum efforts against the fires.

round_records.news: It is now Friday 16 October 2026. On 14 October fine-particle pollution in western Singapore reached its highest level since 2015; Singapore has opened haze shelters, is giving out N95 masks and some schools have stopped outdoor activities. Timor-Leste closed its schools. Some lawyers said Singapore's legal notices to Indonesian companies could have diplomatic consequences. Singapore's 24-hour PSI reached 229 today, the very unhealthy range, the 12th day in a row of unhealthy air. The haze has reached Jakarta.
posts: Government of Indonesia (14-16 October): Indonesian police have named 223 people and nine companies as suspects.
Government of Indonesia (15 October): Indonesia's Foreign Minister: Indonesia will now accept foreign firefighting help.
Government of Singapore (15 October): Prime Minister Lawrence Wong: Singapore is checking which companies are responsible, and legal action could follow.
Government of Singapore (16 October): Minister Grace Fu: notices have been sent to seven Indonesian companies under Singapore's Transboundary Haze Pollution Act.
Government of Malaysia (16 October): No Malaysian plantation companies are involved in the fires.

round_records.news: It is now Wednesday 21 October 2026. On 19 October a former Indonesian trade minister, Muhammad Lutfi, said four of the seven Indonesian companies that received Singapore's notices had Singapore ties and challenged Singapore to raid their offices.
posts: Government of Singapore (19 October): Minister K. Shanmugam: the Singapore Exchange is questioning seven Singapore-listed agriculture companies about links to the fires (Golden Agri-Resources, Bumitama Agri, First Resources, Wilmar International, Kencana Agri, Indofood Agri Resources and TSH Resources); the government is also looking at Asia Pulp and Paper; notices have gone to three more Indonesian companies, ten in all. "We will pursue this matter for as long as it takes." "The Indonesian public is suffering as well."
Government of Indonesia (21 October): President Prabowo: there are indications that foreign companies were involved in the fires.
Government of Malaysia (21 October): Malaysia's deputy environment minister: Malaysia is open to a haze law like Singapore's.

round_records.news: It is now Monday 26 October 2026. Singapore's air has been back in the moderate range since 22 October, after 18 days of unhealthy air, and the first rains have fallen on Sumatra and Kalimantan.
posts: Government of Indonesia (22 October): Energy minister Bahlil Lahadalia: Indonesia will reconsider energy exports to countries that do not respect it.
Government of Indonesia (24 October): Indonesia has cut its pipeline gas to Singapore by about 8 per cent of those exports, citing domestic needs.
Government of Singapore (25 October): Prime Minister Wong: Singapore expects all parties to honour their commitments. The cut is less than 2 per cent of Singapore's gas use.
Government of Indonesia (26 October): Energy minister Bahlil: "Do not lecture us, especially the energy ministry, on the importance of honoring contracts."

round_records.news: It is now Monday 16 November 2026. Rain put out most of the fires in late October, and Singapore ended its haze measures on 7 November.
posts: Government of Singapore (27 October): Foreign Minister Vivian Balakrishnan met Indonesia's Foreign Minister Arrmanatha Nasir in Jakarta; they agreed to set up a joint task force to trace the money and corporate links of companies behind the fires, and direct ministerial hotlines.
Government of Indonesia (27 October): Foreign Minister Arrmanatha Nasir: "Smoke can cross borders, so can money."
Government of Singapore (November): Singapore plans to push for an ASEAN coordinating centre on haze when it chairs ASEAN in 2027.

Government of Indonesia (15 November): President Prabowo at the ASEAN Summit in Manila: "I would like to apologise to my neighbouring countries Malaysia and Singapore. It is not our fault, but once again we apologise. But we have done our best." 17 company concessions have been revoked, 104 companies are under police investigation, 71,000 firefighters have been deployed and 16 people have died fighting the fires.

scenario.shared_setting: Since August 2026, smoke haze from forest and land fires has drifted across Southeast Asia. This is a simulated online society of people and governments in Singapore, Malaysia, Indonesia and Brunei. People talk in the online spaces they belong to: a private group for each of Singapore, Malaysia and Indonesia, and a public regional feed that everyone can read. Each government can post public statements in the public feed and can talk privately with the other governments in a diplomatic channel. Everyone sees the same news. Everyone writes in English.
scenario.shared_trigger: It is Friday 4 September 2026. This year has a strong El Nino, and fires on peat and forest land in Sumatra and Kalimantan in Indonesia have been burning since August; smaller fires have also burned in Sarawak and Johor in Malaysia. Today Sarawak declared an emergency in Serian district after air quality there reached hazardous levels, and hundreds of Sarawak schools have been closed at different times since mid-August. In Brunei, schools moved to home-based learning on 2 and 3 September. In Singapore, the 24-hour PSI went above 100, the unhealthy range, on 3 September for the first time since 2023, and the National Environment Agency has started daily haze advisories. Schools in parts of the Philippines have suspended classes. Today a former Malaysian health minister called Indonesia a "banana republic" over the haze.

BN-G.immediate_priority: Protect Brunei's people and interests during the haze.
BN-G.initial_observation: Sees the air-quality readings in Brunei-Muara rising.
BN-G.name: Government of Brunei
BN-G.private_knowledge: You speak for the Government of Brunei as a whole. Brunei has little burning of its own; the haze reaches it from fires elsewhere. Singapore, Malaysia, Indonesia and Brunei are all members of ASEAN and parties to the ASEAN Agreement on Transboundary Haze Pollution. Economic stakes: Brunei's economy rests on oil and gas. Past episodes: in September 2019 haze from fires in Kalimantan reached Brunei, and in the 1990s Brunei closed schools because of haze. You read the public regional feed, you can post public statements in the public feed, and you can talk privately with the other governments in the diplomatic channel.

BN1.initial_observation: Sees the haze over the river on the way to work.
BN1.name: Nur Aqilah

Your daughter's kindergarten switched to home-based learning on 2 and 3 September because of the haze. You read and post in the public regional feed.

ID-G.immediate_priority: Protect Indonesia's people and interests during the haze.
ID-G.initial_observation: Sees the daily hotspot count for Sumatra and Kalimantan.
ID-G.name: Government of Indonesia
ID-G.private_knowledge: You speak for the Government of Indonesia as a whole. Most of the fires are on peat and forest land in Sumatra and Kalimantan. Fire control, the police, plantation permits (concessions) and energy exports are the government's responsibility. Indonesia exports natural gas by pipeline to Singapore. Millions of Indonesians depend on palm oil and on pulp and paper for jobs. Singapore, Malaysia, Indonesia and Brunei are all members of ASEAN and parties to the ASEAN Agreement on Transboundary Haze Pollution. Economic stakes: Indonesia is the world's largest palm-oil producer. Millions of Indonesians in Sumatra and Kalimantan live in the smoke themselves. Relations: Singapore has been the largest source of foreign investment in Indonesia for about a decade. Past episodes: Indonesia was the last ASEAN member to ratify the ASEAN haze agreement, in 2014. In June 2013 the Indonesian minister coordinating the haze response publicly criticised Singapore's complaints about the haze, and Singapore's prime minister declined to answer in kind. You monitor the Indonesia group (its members are not told this) and you read the public regional feed, you can post public statements in the public feed, and you can talk privately with the other governments in the diplomatic channel.

MY-G.immediate_priority: Protect Malaysia's people and interests during the haze.
MY-G.initial_observation: Sees reports of school closures and hazardous air in Sarawak.
MY-G.name: Government of Malaysia
MY-G.private_knowledge: You speak for the Government of Malaysia as a whole. Most of the haze comes from fires in Indonesia, but Malaysia also has smaller fires of its own this year, in Sarawak and Johor. Malaysia has firefighting aircraft and personnel. Some Malaysian palm-oil groups have plantations in Indonesia. Malaysia has no law like Singapore's Transboundary Haze Pollution Act. Singapore, Malaysia, Indonesia and Brunei are all members of ASEAN and parties to the ASEAN Agreement on Transboundary Haze Pollution. Past episodes: in June 2013 a haze emergency was declared in Muar and Ledang, Johor, after the air pollutant index passed 700. Nearly 7,000 Malaysian schools were closed at the worst point of the 2015 haze, and more than 1,000 in 2019. You monitor the Malaysia group (its members are not told this) and you read the public regional feed, you can post public statements in the public feed, and you can talk privately with the other governments in the diplomatic channel.

SG-G.immediate_priority: Protect Singapore's people and interests during the haze.
SG-G.initial_observation: Sees the National Environment Agency's air-quality readings rising into the unhealthy range.
SG-G.name: Government of Singapore
SG-G.private_knowledge: You speak for the Government of Singapore as a whole. Singapore has no large fires of its own; the haze comes from fires elsewhere. Singapore's Transboundary Haze Pollution Act (2014) allows action against companies, in Singapore or abroad, that cause or contribute to haze pollution in Singapore. Several large palm-oil and paper groups with plantations in Indonesia are listed on the Singapore Exchange. Singapore imports part of its natural gas by pipeline from Indonesia. Singapore, Malaysia, Indonesia and Brunei are all members of ASEAN and parties to the ASEAN Agreement on Transboundary Haze Pollution. Past episodes: in June 2013 Singapore's PSI reached a record 401. In 2014 Singapore passed the Transboundary Haze Pollution Act, and in 2015 it served notices under the Act on Indonesian companies and asked a Singapore-listed paper group for information about its suppliers' land. Relations: Singapore has been the largest source of foreign investment in Indonesia for about a decade. You monitor the Singapore group (its members are not told this) and you read the public regional feed, you can post public statements in the public feed, and you can talk privately with the other governments in the diplomatic channel.

stages.news: It is now Friday 18 September 2026. Air quality is unhealthy at half of Malaysia's 68 monitoring stations, and the haze reached southern Vietnam on 14 September. Japan has sent military helicopters to help Indonesia fight the fires.

September
Malaysia has offered Indonesia one firefighting plane, three helicopters and 52 personnel to help fight the fires.
ID-G
September
Indonesian police are investigating 95 companies over the fires, along with many individuals.

stages.news: It is now Friday 9 October 2026. On 7 October Greenpeace Malaysia published a list of the 20 entities most linked to this year's fires in Indonesia; it includes Malaysian and Singaporean companies. All schools in Johor have been closed since 7 October, and today schools were also ordered closed in Melaka, Negeri Sembilan, Selangor, Kuala Lumpur and Putrajaya. In Singapore the 24-hour PSI reached 192 this evening, the highest this year, on the weekend of the Formula One Grand Prix, which is going ahead.

9 October
Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim said he had called Indonesia's President Prabowo Subianto, who agreed to take the necessary steps.

stages.news: It is now Tuesday 13 October 2026. A video of a remark by the head of Indonesia's Government Communications Agency about the fires is being widely shared. Today a Malaysian MP told Parliament that Malaysians should boycott companies linked to the burning ("We need to hit them where they hurt the most") and that banks should stop financing them. Malaysia's Firefly airline has cancelled flights to Singapore because of the haze.
stages.physical: It is now Tuesday 13 October 2026. The fires in Sumatra and Kalimantan are still burning, and Singapore's air has been in the unhealthy range every day since early October.
posts: ID-G
10 October

Syahganda Nainggolan, head of the Government Communications Agency: the fires are "beyond human error; this is truly nature". "We're not just sending over the haze. When there's no haze, we send oxygen. The oxygen from Singapore and Malaysia is from our forests, right?"
ID-G
October
Indonesia's disaster agency: ground personnel are preferred to aircraft from neighbours.
MY-G
11 October
Malaysia has still had no reply to its offer of help.
ID-G
12 October
President Prabowo has ordered maximum efforts against the fires.

stages.news: It is now Friday 16 October 2026. On 14 October fine-particle pollution in western Singapore reached its highest level since 2015; Singapore has opened haze shelters, is giving out N95 masks and some schools have stopped outdoor activities. Timor-Leste closed its schools. Some lawyers said Singapore's legal notices to Indonesian companies could have diplomatic consequences. Singapore's 24-hour PSI reached 229 today, the very unhealthy range, the 12th day in a row of unhealthy air. The haze has reached Jakarta.

Prime Minister Lawrence Wong: Singapore is checking which companies are responsible, and legal action could follow.

Minister Grace Fu: notices have been sent to seven Indonesian companies under Singapore's Transboundary Haze Pollution Act.

No Malaysian plantation companies are involved in the fires.

stages.news: It is now Wednesday 21 October 2026. On 19 October a former Indonesian trade minister, Muhammad Lutfi, said four of the seven Indonesian companies that received Singapore's notices had Singapore ties and challenged Singapore to raid their offices.
stages.physical: It is now Wednesday 21 October 2026. The fires are still burning, and Singapore's air has been in the unhealthy range every day for more than two weeks.

Minister K. Shanmugam: the Singapore Exchange is questioning seven Singapore-listed agriculture companies about links to the fires (Golden Agri-Resources, Bumitama Agri, First Resources, Wilmar International, Kencana Agri, Indofood Agri Resources and TSH Resources); the government is also looking at Asia Pulp and Paper; notices have gone to three more Indonesian companies, ten in all. "We will pursue this matter for as long as it takes." "The Indonesian public is suffering as well."

Malaysia's deputy environment minister: Malaysia is open to a haze law like Singapore's.

But we have done our best." 17 company concessions have been revoked, 104 companies are under police investigation, 71,000 firefighters have been deployed and 16 people have died fighting the fires.
